articleTitle: L-band MMIC active filter techniques for future satellite payloads
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Recent Advances in Microwave Sub-Systems for Space and Satellite Applications
abstract: The authors describe the realisation of MMIC bandpass active filters for space applications, with target filter design specifications in the L-band. In the microwave frequency region, active filters can offer many significant advantages such as compensation for losses accompanied with passive elements and the possibility of having positive gain rather than loss. In addition, if these filters are realised as MMIC it would be advantageous not only because of their compact size but also because of their consistency with other well established circuits such as amplifiers, mixers, and phase shifters. The authors describe two different active filter approaches: the cascaded cells approach, where passive resonators are coupled together by active devices to prevent them interacting; and the use of FET-based active inductors to replace passive inductors in integrated circuit filters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Monolithic phase shifter for S-band inter-satellite data relay antenna
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Recent Advances in Microwave Sub-Systems for Space and Satellite Applications
abstract: The author reports the design and measurement of a five-bit, switched filter, MMIC phase shifter. The circuit achieves a small r.m.s. phase shift error, low insertion loss and minimal insertion loss variation over the 2.2-2.3 GHz design band.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A high performance analogue time shifter for wideband phased array antennas
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Recent Advances in Microwave Sub-Systems for Space and Satellite Applications
abstract: A purely analogue reflection-type time shifter is presented. Quick design equations are given that enable a traditional reflection-type phase shifter topology to emulate a true time shifter. Simulated results for an X-band design demonstrate that a high performance can be achieved over at least a 40% bandwidth, when a 3 dB Lange coupler is employed. This novel time shifter offers considerable advantages over conventional classes of time shifter, which makes it ideally suitable for high performance applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Asymmetric E-plane bandpass filters with improved stopband performance
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Recent Advances in Microwave Sub-Systems for Space and Satellite Applications
abstract: Summary form only given. A computer aided design method has been developed to synthesise E-plane bandpass filters with improved stopband performance. The predicted filter performance showing improved stopband performance and reduced filter dimensions compared with conventional E-plane bandpass filters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An antenna simulator system for satellite communications adaptive digital beam forming network
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Recent Advances in Microwave Sub-Systems for Space and Satellite Applications
abstract: An antenna simulator system has been developed, under a contract from European Space Agency (ESA), to evaluate the performance of an adaptive digital beam forming network (ADBFN), which was designed and constructed under the same contract. The system architecture is described. Measurements showed that a typical phase accuracy of +or-1 degree was achieved with this system for a single 5 MHz IF channel.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: MMIC components for X- and Ku-band satellite systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Recent Advances in Microwave Sub-Systems for Space and Satellite Applications
abstract: The authors describe the design and performance of a range of MMIC components suitable for satellite systems operating in X- and Ku-band. The chips have all been fabricated with the GEC-Marconi (Caswell) standard F20 foundry process, which provides 0.5 mu m gate-length ion-implanted MESFETs, and through-GaAs via-holes. The circuits described are: a small-signal amplifier for use as a front-end gain block, a balanced amplifier suitable for a transmitter predriver chain, a 1 W power amplifier, an analogue phase shifter, a mixer suitable for receivers and up-converters, and finally a VCO suitable for integration into a phase-locked oscillator subsystem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: S-band high isolation switch for space and satellite applications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Recent Advances in Microwave Sub-Systems for Space and Satellite Applications
abstract: Shunt series monolithic PIN diodes are used in a number of different thin film, planar circuits to achieve very low loss in the ON state and very high isolation in the OFF state. The switch unit was realised in a number of different configurations and the effects of different design arrangements on insertion loss and isolation are studied. The planar microwave switch was realised both in microstrip and coplanar waveguide media.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An adaptive quadrature phase QPSK modulator with a C-band IF for VSAT system applications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Recent Advances in Microwave Sub-Systems for Space and Satellite Applications
abstract: The author describes the development of a QPSK modulator operating with a 4 GHz IF to enable implementation of terminals with minimal frequency conversion and RF processing configurations for VSAT systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: GaAs MMIC frequency upconverters for satellite applications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Recent Advances in Microwave Sub-Systems for Space and Satellite Applications
abstract: A Ku-band MMIC upconverter with unwanted local oscillator and lower sideband signal suppression has been designed. The various possible solutions and trade-offs in the design of FET upconverter building blocks are discussed. Simulated electrical performance characteristics of the upconverter are presented. Final layout using standard foundry components is also included.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
